summary.headline: A few patterns are worth a conversation — close dates cluster on period ends and optional fields go unfilled — but these are signals to investigate, not conclusions.
summary.narrative: These are signals to investigate with curiosity, not accusations against any rep. We see close dates clustering on quarter/month ends and next steps populated only where they seem to be enforced. Patterns like these usually point to incentives and process, not bad actors — start there before changing the system, and never feed un-investigated patterns to an AI as truth.

stats.label: Close dates on a period end

findings.title: Signal to investigate: close dates cluster on month/quarter ends
findings.what_we_found: Several open and recent deals carry close dates on period boundaries: OPP-2002 and OPP-2016 on 2026-01-31, OPP-2006 on 2025-12-31, OPP-2007 closed 2025-12-20. This is a pattern to explore, not evidence of anything.
findings.why_it_blocks_ai: If close dates are set by the calendar rather than the deal, an AI forecasting on them learns the calendar, not reality. Worth understanding before an AI consumes close dates.
the_fix: Investigate with the team why dates land on period ends — it may be genuine procurement timing.
Check whether forecasting incentives encourage end-of-period bunching.
Treat this as a discussion starter, not a verdict on any rep.

findings.title: Signal to investigate: optional fields filled only where seemingly required
findings.what_we_found: next_step is consistently populated on early-stage outbound deals with booked calls but blank on several mid/late-stage deals (OPP-2003, OPP-2006, OPP-2013, OPP-2019), hinting reps may fill fields only where enforced. This is a hypothesis to check, not a finding of fault.
findings.why_it_blocks_ai: If fields are completed only under enforcement, the data reflects the rule set, not the deal — an AI would mistake compliance for signal.
the_fix: Investigate whether the blanks track a missing validation rule rather than rep intent.
Make the field genuinely useful (and required where it matters) so completion is honest, not forced.
Confirm the pattern with the team before drawing any conclusion.
findings.evidence: Blank next_step concentrated on later-stage deals.

findings.title: Recommendation: align incentives before policing the data
findings.what_we_found: The patterns above commonly trace back to how reps are measured — pull-forward credit, period-end quota pressure, or fields tied to compensation gates.
findings.why_it_blocks_ai: Policing the data without fixing the incentive just moves the gaming elsewhere; an AI built on incentive-distorted data inherits the distortion.
the_fix: Review comp and forecast incentives against the behaviours these signals hint at.
Make accurate, complete data the path of least resistance for reps.
Re-run this assessment after incentive changes to see if the signals fade.
findings.evidence: Patterns above are consistent with period-driven incentives.

disclaimers: These are signals to investigate, not conclusions about any individual. Patterns can have legitimate explanations; confirm with the team before acting.
